method: All measurements are on Rec.601 luma of the full-resolution files. Paper mask throughout is (luma > 150) & ((R - B) < 40); desk mask is the complement, dilated 3 px, with (R - B) > 25. Clips were decoded with toolchain/ffmpeg/ffmpeg piping rawvideo to numpy; no PNGs were written to the repo. Every number below names the file and the pixel box it came from.

findings.where: the desk to the right of the 'off until saturday' sheet. Sheet paper region y 1577-2620, x 79-1345; the dark region's bbox is y 1594-2495, x 921-1348
findings.what: A single connected region of 113,175 px (2.52 per cent of the 1440x3120 frame) sits below luma 30 on the desk beside one flat sheet: mean luma 25.4, max 29.97, widest row 219 px (55 CSS px at 4x). Walking right from the sheet's own edge the desk stays below luma 60 for 171 of the first 200 px and has still not recovered at +250 px (64.2 against a desk baseline of 91.8 measured at x 1395-1420, y 1650-2450). Walking DOWN from the same sheet in the same frame: minimum 56.8 at +5 px, below 60 for only 4 px, back to 90.7 by +250 px. Four pixels below and 171 pixels to the right, on one sheet, under one light. And the slab does not answer the light: in crops/dusk_pulse.png the same mask reads 33.5 against a desk of 118.5, a ratio of 0.283 against the day's 0.277, while the desk under it moved 27 grey levels.
findings.why: The row requires 'contact shadows baked from the render's own lighting rather than applied as a uniform blur'. A fixed multiply 55 CSS px wide that is identical under both lighting conditions is neither baked nor a contact shadow; at that scale the sheet reads as floating about two and a half centimetres above the desk. logs/holes.json names the mechanism (a nine-sliced shadow whose opaque core is exposed wherever it fails to line up with its piece), reports beside_the_paper 14190 for this still and sets ok:false, so the build knows and it is still the first screen a reader sees.

findings.where: the bottom edge of the 'four left' note (paper y 2345-2633, x 154-1208), and the top edge of the photo note (paper y 282-907, x 234-594)
findings.what: 98.6 per cent of the 'four left' note's bottom-edge columns terminate at exactly y = 2633 (100 per cent over the middle 60 per cent of its width); luma goes 177.96 at y 2633 to 79.37 at y 2634 in one pixel, averaged over x 200-1149. Below the cut: three rows at 79.4 / 79.4 / 78.2, then a one-pixel step to 89.3 and a flat 90.6 desk - a 3 px hard-edged band. On the same screen the big note's bottom edge (y 1559-2019, x 151-1227) falls to 66.8 at +4..+8 px and recovers monotonically to the 90.1 desk over about 32 px, a real penumbra. Measured on four sides, the 'four left' note's 'below' shadow reads 2.50 grey levels against 15.80-20.76 for every other note in the frame. The same clip rectangle cuts the photo note's top dead straight at y = 282 for 100 per cent of its middle 60 per cent, while the leftmost ~120 px of that identical edge (x 234-360) is visibly torn with fibres. Twenty-three rows of desk are visible between the cut at 2633 and the composer's torn top at 2660, so the sheet is seen to stop dead in the middle of the wood.
findings.why: The row is judged at three hundred per cent on the Chat hero, and at that zoom a sheet that ends in a razor-straight line with a 3 px dark stroke instead of a tear and a shadow reads as a rectangle with a texture in it rather than as a photograph of paper. logs/hairline.json checks for a row BRIGHTER than both its neighbours and reports 0 for all ten stills; this fault is a row darker than both, which that check cannot see, so nothing in the record catches it.

findings.where: the ten measurable torn edges on the Chat hero; the extremes are at y ~1510 and y ~1270, x 400-820
findings.what: Taking the first paper pixel down each column over the middle 80 per cent of each piece and high-passing over 31 columns, the edge roughness in px rms is: texthome.bottom 1.165, bignote.top 1.480, voice.top 1.625, fourleft.top 1.798, bignote.bottom 1.886, photonote.bottom 2.050, compose.bottom 3.007, compose.top 3.030, voice.bottom 4.136, texthome.top 4.888. Five of ten are under 2.0. At 300 per cent the 1.165 edge is a straight line with a fringe on it; the 4.888 edge from the same screen is a ragged silhouette with deep notches.
findings.why: logs/torn.json sets the calibration itself - 'a critic measured the note edges they were content with at rms 2.88 to 5.14 on the glass and the ones they were not at 0.36 to 0.59. Half this library is under 2' - names the cause (tools/tears/tear.py, the fracture's Hurst exponent running to 1.15, 'a clean pull is too clean') and states it was not re-rendered this cycle. My count on the hero (5 of 10) matches the library's own (28 of 56 masks under 2 px rms). The row asks for tear masks; half of what is on the hero is a clean cut with a frayed fringe.

findings.where: inside the big note, paper y 1559-2019, x 151-1227; the clearest pair is y 1712-1758 at x 937-968 and x 1037-1068
findings.what: I took the 67 ink connected components of 120 px or more inside that one note and matched each against every other at NATIVE scale (no normalisation to a common box, plus or minus 3 px search, sizes required to agree within 2 px): median best-match IoU 0.766, p90 0.936, max 0.957, and 23 of 67 marks (34 per cent) have a twin at IoU >= 0.85. The clearest case is two components on the SAME line 100 px apart - the two 'p's of 'laptop' - at IoU 0.934, with the same bowl, the same descender curvature and the same terminal. Pressure is present but weak: on the ink ridge (distance transform > 1 px, n = 3098) stroke half-width is mean 2.01 px, p5 1.41, p95 3.00, CV 0.225, and the correlation between half-width and ink luma is only -0.130, where a real pen presses wider and darker together.
findings.why: The row asks for 'handwriting with multiple variants per glyph and real pressure variance'. logs/fonts.json shows the variants exist (NoorHand and TeoHand carry five per glyph over 775 glyphs) but its own twin share is 0.3006 against the 0.2 that five variants picked uniformly would give, so the picker repeats itself half again as often as chance - and at 300 per cent that lands as an indistinguishable twin roughly every third mark. hand.json's 0.196 twin share is measured after normalising every mark to one box, which is a weaker test than the one the rubric asks a reader to apply.

findings.where: logs/lines.json; on the hero, the big note's rules at y 1599 / 1680 / 1761 / 1841, x 200-1150
findings.what: logs/lines.json measures the set at a median 0.309 of the rule pitch away from the nearest rule, where writing laid out with no relation to the rules averages 0.25; 02_chat reads 0.333 over 24 lines, 10_first_run 0.423, 13_messenger_states 0.421. My own check on the hero note is kinder than the set: the rules sit at a pitch of 80.7 px and the three written baselines land 15, 6 and 16 px above the nearest rule, i.e. 0.19, 0.07 and 0.20 of a pitch. It is visible in crops/02_chat_300_hand.png, where the writing floats above the rule and only the descenders reach it.
findings.why: The rubric judges whether the paper reads as photographed, and writing that hovers a few points above the ruling it was supposedly written on is the tell that the type was laid over a picture of paper rather than onto it. lines.json is honest that this is neither gated nor fixed, and says why (the stock is scaled to the piece while the text is scaled to its point size); on the hero itself the offset is small enough to be a minor rather than a serious fault.

findings.what: Each region report names a stock whose paper never arrived: spiral_03 in 02_chat, sticky_blue_02 in 01_pulse and 04_moments; 02_chat also reports paper_that_arrived_after_the_piece_was_drawn = 92. Per BRIEFING.md a piece whose stock has not arrived paints the flat colour under it. Nothing flat is visible: logs/flat.json reports files_with_a_flat_fill 0 and sheets_with_no_paper_on_them [] for all ten stills, and my own flat-shape test on the final frames of 15_authored_feeling.mp4, 07_feeling_landing.mp4 and 08_state_propagating.mp4 (pale, local 9 px sd under 0.35) finds no connected flat shape over 2000 px in any of them.
findings.why: The anti-goal that fails the whole visual concept is a flat fill standing in for paper, and this build has a live path to one. It did not fire on the glass in this capture, which is why this is minor rather than blocking, but a piece on the Chat hero was drawn over a stock that never came.

what_is_working: No tear repeats on a single screen, which is the row's headline requirement. Over the ten torn edges on 02_chat.png the best pairwise normalised cross-correlation at ANY lag is 0.343 (bignote.top against voice.top); everything else is under 0.33. No edge repeats inside itself either: the worst self-correlation past the central lobe is 0.263 (voice.top). logs/torn.json records that the two-sine shape this replaced scored 0.72 to 0.81 on the same measurement.

One consistent light direction across the whole set. Desk luma at 4-12 px out from a piece minus the same at 40-60 px out, over every paper region above 40,000 px, in all nine day stills: below 6.7 to 20.1, right 6.0 to 10.5, above -2.9 to +1.0, left -1.8 to +4.4. A single key from the upper left, with no piece anywhere disagreeing.

Contact shadows with a real penumbra where the shadow lines up with its piece. 02_chat.png big note bottom edge, averaged over x 151-1227: 170.7 on the paper, 66.8 at +4..+8 px, then a monotone recovery to the 90.1 desk by +32 px. That is a baked soft shadow, not a uniform blur at a fixed offset.

The stock is photographed, not procedural, on three independent measurements. (1) Between four sheets on 02_chat.png the high-passed grain cross-correlates at 0.104 to 0.131, against a self-control of 1.0000 - every sheet carries different fibre. (2) No tiling: the autocorrelation of a clean paper patch has a best off-centre peak of 0.219 to 0.238 at short lags with no harmonic, where a tiled texture would peak near 1.0 at the tile period. (3) The grain is mapped to the paper rather than painted on the screen - between frames 96 and 97 of 06_unfolding.mp4 the sheet moves 3 px and the grain matches at r = 0.925 at dy = -3 against r = 0.103 at dy = 0.

The fold is rendered geometry catching light, not a flat image being transformed. 06_unfolding.mp4 frame 96, rows 1180-1239 averaged over x 200-650: the flat panel sits at 240.8, rises through a specular crease ridge peaking at 246.5, falls to a trough of 229.5, lifts to a secondary lobe at 234.7, then settles onto the shaded panel at 207.3 - a 35 px fillet with a highlight and a shadow on it, where a warped bitmap would give a step. The panel ratio tracks the fold angle (0.855 at frame 96, 0.727 at frame 112), the sheet shows its own thickness at the leading edge, and the cast shadow on the desk falls down and to the right, matching the stills. logs/surfaces.json confirms the source: fold_sequences.unfold_thirds, 142 rendered frames, worst 3.079 against a floor of 1.2, none below it.

Feelings are physical objects, not icons. 01_pulse.png y 1190-1440: confetti is a scatter of individual paper scraps with thickness, curl and their own lower-right contact shadows; hold is a soft body with an upper-left specular and lower-right shading; nyeh is a wrapped sweet with soft-body creases. logs/surfaces.json counts 62 object surfaces, 34 of them named by feelings, with flat, unlit, too_small_to_measure and empty all empty lists.

The paper keeps its tooth through a fling. 11_chat_scroll.mp4, clean 40x80 patches with luma between 205 and 252: high-pass sd median 1.07 at frame 0 and 1.01 / 1.09 / 1.07 / 0.98 / 0.94 at frames 60, 120, 180, 210 and 240. No smearing or resample collapse mid-scroll.

Nothing in the set is a stale still. MANIFEST.json marks every artifact from_this_run true except logs/apk.json, and DIFF.json gives every artifact an ssim under 0.999 against the previous capture, so none of them is a picture of an older build.

not_worth_opening.reason: 14_media_viewer_strip.png I did not open: the media viewer's material question is whether its large flat areas are a paper stand-in, and that is answered on the full-resolution still (which I did open) plus logs/flat.json, which names the eight flat shapes, gives their colours (#E5E6EB, #DFE2E9, #D8DBE4 and similar - bluish, none of them one of the app's warm paper fallback fills) and shows they are the sky and water of a photograph. A six-frame strip adds no material evidence the still does not already carry.

A vibration vocabulary and its felt-distance derivation. I opened crops/haptics_strip.png to see what they describe and it is a timing chart, not a surface; nothing in either file bears on whether paper reads as photographed.

not_worth_opening.path: evidence/logs/pwa.json, evidence/logs/webpush.txt, evidence/logs/manifest-adjacent install records, evidence/logs/apk.json
not_worth_opening.reason: Installability and packaging. logs/apk.json is also the one check MANIFEST.json marks from_this_run false, which is a finding for whoever reads the reliability row; it says nothing about a surface.
78 KB of the app's copy. It is the anti-goal critic's evidence for voice and the coherence critic's for wording; no measurement in it describes a material.

Per-frame build and raster cost, and the thread's own record of how far each throw asked it to move. Performance, not material. I judged the scroll's material integrity directly off the clip instead, by measuring paper tooth at rest and mid-fling.
The notification pocket and what the phone was still holding when picked up. The briefing says outright these are not artifacts; they record platform state, not a surface.

not_worth_opening.path: evidence/reliability.json, evidence/coldstart.json, evidence/logs/tests.log, evidence/logs/<scene>.json step logs
not_worth_opening.reason: Wall-clock cost, load breakdowns and harness step timings. The briefing is explicit that the wall-clock interval between grabs is the harness's cost of taking the picture; none of it can show whether a surface is photographed.

The shooting scripts. I would have opened one had I needed to tell a fault in the app from a fault in the framing, but the two faults I am gating on - a 113,175 px slab beside a sheet, and a sheet ending in a razor-straight line with 23 rows of desk visible below it - are on the glass whatever the scene asked for.

The capture before this one. DIFF.json already tells me every artifact changed (ssim 0.675 to 0.926) and MANIFEST.json that all are from this run, so nothing here is stale; reading the previous capture would only tell me whether a fault is new, which is build history and not mine to know.
Another reader's conclusions. Found and left closed, as the briefing requires.

My prompt says the material row is judged from artifacts. Where a log names a source file as the cause - tools/tears/tear.py for the Hurst exponent, blender/paper/rules.py for the rulings - I quoted the log rather than opening the file.

verdict: The hard parts of this row are genuinely done and I could measure them: no tear mask repeats on a single screen (worst pairwise cross-correlation between the ten torn edges on the Chat hero is 0.343, worst self-correlation past the central lobe 0.263, against 0.72-0.81 for the shape this replaced); the stock is real scanned paper on three independent tests (grain cross-correlates at 0.104-0.131 between sheets against a self-control of 1.0, no tiling peak above 0.238, and the grain travels with the sheet at r=0.925 when it moves 3 px rather than sitting still in screen space at r=0.103); the unfolding clip is rendered geometry, with a 35 px crease fillet carrying a specular ridge at 246.5 and a trough at 229.5 between two panels at 240.8 and 207.3; the light is one key from the upper left in every one of the nine day stills; and the feelings are lit objects with their own contact shadows, not icons. None of the three faults the rubric says score this category below its floor - a procedural noise overlay, a tiled repeating texture, a beige rounded rectangle - is present, and I looked for all three. What holds the row under its floor is the sixth thing the rubric names. On 01_pulse.png, the first screen of the app, a 113,175-pixel slab at mean luma 25.4 - two and a half per cent of the frame, 55 CSS px wide at its widest - sits on the desk beside one flat sheet, while that same sheet's bottom edge four pixels away casts a correct 4 px contact shadow; and the slab reads at the same 0.28 multiply in crops/dusk_pulse.png, unchanged when the light changes, which is the definition of a shadow not baked from the render's own lighting. That is the blocking finding. Two more would have to move before the row clears: on the Chat hero the scroll's clip rectangle guillotines sheets - 98.6 per cent of the 'four left' note's bottom columns end at exactly y=2633, replacing a tear and a 30 px penumbra with a razor line and a 3 px hard stroke, with 23 rows of desk visible below it - and half the torn edges on that same hero (five of ten under rms 2.0) sit in the band logs/torn.json itself calls a clean pull, a fault the build has measured, diagnosed to tools/tears/tear.py, and chosen not to re-render this cycle. Twenty-one.
